concerns.text: The plan acknowledges that a detectable ΔMAE = 0.2 requires N ≈ 210 samples, yet the curated dataset contains only 20 molecules. This sample size is far too small to achieve adequate statistical power for the paired t‑test/Wilcoxon analysis, making any claim of statistical significance (p < 0.05) unreliable.

The evaluation pipeline performs a paired t‑test (or Wilcoxon) on per‑molecule error differences despite the extremely limited N=20. With such a tiny sample, the normality assumption is dubious and effect‑size estimates (Cohen’s d, 95 % CI) will be highly unstable, undermining construct validity of the performance comparison.

Robustness checks (multi‑seed training, L2 sweep) are planned, but with only 20 data points the variance estimates (target < 0.01 MAE variance) are unlikely to be meaningful; the dataset does not provide enough diversity to assess generalizability.

While a scaffold split prevents scaffold leakage, applying it to a 20‑molecule set can produce splits with very few scaffolds per split, leading to high variance and potential over‑fitting. The plan does not include a mitigation (e.g., repeated random splits) to address this.
